name: @reviewplane/server
description: ReviewPlane control-plane server: the authoritative HTTP API for projects, connectors, published services, browser sessions, artefacts, reviews, findings, agent sessions and events.

./testing.//: Test infrastructure only, and deliberately reachable only under the development condition: a disposable PostgreSQL belongs in a test run and never in a build output. apps/mcp-server runs against the same database as apps/server, so a second copy of this helper would be a second thing to keep in step with the migrations.

./testing/config.//: The one complete ServerConfig for tests. A second copy in another package would be a second thing to update when a setting is added.

./testing/tls.//: A loopback listener certificate and its ADR-0015 pin, issued by the product's own X.509 code so a test cannot pass against a shape the product would refuse.

./testing/publishing.//: The route publisher and tunnel gateway doubles, so a test that needs a published service does not need a connector and a gateway process.

scripts.//cli: The operator command line of docs/DEPLOYMENT.md section 11. The deployed image exposes it as `reviewplane`; in a checkout it is run through this script, which needs no build. A `bin` entry would make pnpm try to link dist/cli.js at install time, before anything has been built.
scripts.//test:security: The standing security gates this package owns (docs/TESTING.md section 10). They are also matched by `test` above, so they run on every change; this runs them alone. Membership is the `security-gate-` filename prefix rather than a list, so a gate added here is a gate this script runs. The prefix is deliberately specific: a `-gate` suffix also matches `completion-gate.test.ts`, which is a domain rule and not a security gate. The `ls` is a guard, not decoration. `node --test` exits 0 when its glob matches nothing — verified: `pass 0, fail 0`, exit 0 — so a renamed file or a broken pattern would make this script report green having executed nothing, and it is the named owner of two docs/TESTING.md section 16 conditions. `ls` fails on a pattern that matches no file, so an empty run is a failure rather than a pass. RVP-106 tracks the same hole in the other suites' scripts.
